world.title: ZAMBIA: Bishop Lungu Calls for Dialogue, Justice and Reconciliation in Zambia
world.description:
By Sandra Kunda
The Bishop of Chipata Diocese, Rt. Rev. George Cosmas Zumaire Lungu has called for prayer, dialogue, justice and reconciliation amid growing concerns over the political situation in Zambia.
In a pastoral statement issued on September 15, 2026, Bishop Lungu said recent events in the country have caused concern and uncertainty among citizens, stressing the need to uphold human dignity, the rule of law, access to justice and the rights of every citizen.
The Bishop particularly cited the closure of court premises on August 24, 2026, which coincided with the final day for filing constitutional challenges to the presidential election results.
He said the development had raised concerns among citizens regarding access to justice and the protection of constitutional rights.
Bishop Lungu said the Catholic Church does not take sides in political contests, but can not remain silent when justice, peace, human dignity and the rule of law are threatened.
He has proposed a respectful and private dialogue with the President and representatives of Government to discuss concerns surrounding justice, the rule of law, political tolerance and the treatment of opposition figures.
The Bishop has also invited Church leaders, traditional leaders, professionals, young people, academics, civil society actors and other concerned citizens to a preparatory meeting to reflect on how they can contribute to peace, justice and reconciliation.
Bishop Lungu has since urged Zambians to move beyond political divisions and embrace forgiveness and reconciliation, saying political differences should not become a source of hatred, intimidation or violence.
END

science.title: Harmonised climate and Aedes albopictus arboviral vector mosquito surveillance datasets for the European continent
science.description: We present two harmonised datasets linking Aedes albopictus mosquito surveillance observations with standardised climate variables, designed to support benchmarking and reproducible modelling of mosquito distribution and abundance across Europe. The first dataset pairs polygon-level presence/absence records from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) with ERA5-Land and CORDEX climate grids, yielding 157,918 and 79,398 spatially explicit grid points respectively, of which 34,482 and 20,832 carry confirmed presence labels. The second dataset combines 15,374 trap-level observations from 1,648 trap locations across western and southern Europe (AIMSurv v2.3) with ERA5-Land daily and monthly climate variables aligned to sampling periods. Both datasets are generated through transparent, documented preprocessing pipelines with explicit quality-control criteria, relying exclusively on open data sources. Rather than introducing new primary surveillance observations, this secondary data resource provides a reproducible transformation of public surveillance and climate sources into common, analysis-ready benchmark datasets. Together, they provide a consistent foundation for methodological benchmarking and reuse across ecological and epidemiological applications. Both datasets are publicly available via the JRC Data Catalogue.
